Description

How long ERK stays active decides what the cell does, and the product of an immediate early gene, c-Fos, reads that duration. ERK phosphorylates the transcription factor ELK1, which then forms a ternary complex with SRF on the serum response element of the FOS gene and activates it [1, 2]. Sustained ERK signalling prolongs the expression of FOS and of other immediate early genes [3]. The c-Fos protein made after a brief pulse of ERK is unstable and soon degraded. When ERK signalling lasts, the still-active ERK and RSK phosphorylate the C-terminus of c-Fos on Ser362 and Ser374, which stabilises it [4-6]. This phosphorylation exposes a docking site for ERK, the DEF domain, through which ERK phosphorylates c-Fos further on Thr325 and Thr331 and raises its transcriptional activity [4, 7]. c-Fos therefore accumulates only when ERK activity outlasts the induction of its gene. How much the C-terminal phosphorylation stabilises c-Fos depends on the state of the cell [8].
